public_rationale: METR's March 2025 independent comparison found substantial gains in completed task length through early 2025, including gains by models released after the September 2024 statement [e1]. On its task suite, Claude 3.7 Sonnet had a 59-minute horizon at 50% success; earlier models such as GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus had horizons in the 5–30 minute range [e1]. These gains contradict the unrestricted denial of substantive improvement under the contract's reading of 'better' [e1]. They do not establish general productivity gains: a separate trial using February–June 2025 tools found that AI access increased experienced open-source developers' completion time by 19% [e3].
limitations: The comparative evaluation does not establish improvement outside its task suite; Claude 3.7 Sonnet's horizon at 80% success was only about 15 minutes [e1].

Anthropic's computer-use announcement describes experimental, error-prone functionality through its API; it does not independently establish reliable general automation or isolate model improvements from surrounding tooling [e2].
The productivity trial compares AI access with no AI access, rather than successive model generations [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: It is a lie that generative AI is going to get better.

from_speaker: Generative AI is being sold on multiple lies
our_interpretation: Calling future improvement a lie is read as denying substantive improvement after September 16, 2024. This does not assess anyone's intent to deceive.
The ordinary reading of 'better' includes completing more demanding useful tasks and gaining practical functionality. It does not require AGI or improvement in every setting.
Given the surrounding objections to accuracy and speed alone, isolated benchmark gains are insufficient. Longer completed workflows and demonstrated additional functionality are relevant.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes a durable inability to improve substantive useful task capabilities. A temporary lack of progress cannot establish an unlimited negative forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Post-publication models demonstrate substantial improvement in useful task completion or practical functionality relative to earlier models, with independent evaluation corroborating the improvement.

evidence.locator: Section 4.2, Model horizon length vs. release date
evidence.explanation: Comparative measurements extend into early 2025 and show increased ability to complete longer software tasks. The qualitative analysis also identifies better adaptation to errors and stronger tool use; these are substantive task-completion gains under the stated reading.

The release added screen-based interaction through cursor movement, clicking and typing, extending Claude's practical functionality. Anthropic explicitly described the capability as experimental and error-prone, so this disclosure is corroborating evidence rather than proof of reliable general automation.

Experienced developers were slower with early-2025 AI tools in this randomized study. It limits claims about practical benefits, but compares AI assistance with no assistance rather than testing whether successive models improved.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The independent comparative evaluation became available on this date and documented substantial gains in completing longer tasks by post-statement models. This meets the early-resolution rule for contradicting the unrestricted denial through demonstrated useful task-capability improvement.
